title: Lemma 2.5: AFP projection identities $\lambda_1(e_B)+\lambda_2(e_B)=1+e_B$ and the key operator inequalities

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Proof of Lemma 2.5 (AFP base lemma), final paragraph.

The contradiction uses, without proof:
1. $\lambda_1(e_B)+\lambda_2(e_B)=1+e_B$, where $\lambda_i(e_B)$ projects onto vectors of $L^2(M_1\ast_B M_2)$ "beginning in $M_{i+1}^o$ or $B$" ([TY25, Prop. 4.16]).
2. $u_1^*\lambda_1(e_B)u_1+u_2^*\lambda_1(e_B)u_2\le\lambda_2(e_B)$ and $u_3^*\lambda_2(e_B)u_3\le\lambda_1(e_B)$.

Identity (1) is a structural fact about the AFP $L^2$-space and needs a reduced-word proof. Inequalities (2) are **exactly where the hypotheses $E_B(u_1)=E_B(u_2)=E_B(u_3)=E_B(u_1^*u_2)=0$ are used**: they guarantee that $u_1\xi,u_2\xi$ are orthogonal and that left multiplication by $u_i$ raises word-length appropriately, mapping $\lambda_2$-vectors into $\lambda_1$-vectors (and vice versa). These must be derived explicitly, verifying each $E_B$-vanishing hypothesis at the point of use.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
## Critic notes on the current proof of the AFP operator identities

**(eq:lam-sum) $\lambda_1(e_B)+\lambda_2(e_B)=1+e_B$ — correct.** Decompose $L^2M=A_1\oplus A_2\oplus L^2B$ (words beginning in $M_1^o$, in $M_2^o$, and $L^2B$). Then $\operatorname{ran}\lambda_1(e_B)=A_2\oplus L^2B$ and $\operatorname{ran}\lambda_2(e_B)=A_1\oplus L^2B$, so the sum is $A_1\oplus A_2\oplus 2\cdot L^2B=1+e_B$. ✓

**(eq:tree) first inequality — ERROR (see separate issue prob-10-10).** As written it uses conjugation by $u_j^{*}$ ($u_j^{*}\lambda_1 u_j$), whose orthogonality of the two summand ranges requires $E_B(u_2u_1^{*})=0$, NOT the stated hypothesis $E_B(u_1^{*}u_2)=0$. This genuinely fails in main-theorem Case B (there $u_2u_1^{*}=b\,a_w a_w^{*}=b\in B$, so $E_B(u_2u_1^{*})=b\neq0$). The correct form is conjugation by $u_j$:
$$u_1\lambda_1(e_B)u_1^{*}+u_2\lambda_1(e_B)u_2^{*}\le\lambda_2(e_B),$$
for which orthogonality follows from $E_B(u_2^{*}u_1)=E_B(u_1^{*}u_2)^{*}=0$. Full details in **prob-10-10**.

**(eq:tree) second inequality $u_3\lambda_2 u_3^{*}\le\lambda_1$ — fine** (single inclusion, no orthogonality needed; either conjugation direction works).

**Step-3 evaluation** $2a\le b\le a$, $a+b=1\Rightarrow$ contradiction is correct *provided* the corrected (eq:tree) and Step 1 ($\varphi(\iota^\sharp(e_B))=0$, see prob-10-7) hold.
